nodes.t: C-01 Absolute basics: syntax, types, control flow (weeks 1 to 3)

nodes.t: C-02 Arrays, strings and the C standard library (weeks 4 to 5)

nodes.t: C-03 Structs, unions, bitfields: the kernel building blocks (weeks 6 to 8)

nodes.t: C-04 Preprocessor, macros and kernel-style C (weeks 9 to 10)

nodes.t: M-01 Pointers: address arithmetic and dereferencing (weeks 11 to 13)

nodes.t: M-02 Dynamic memory: malloc, the heap and kernel allocators (weeks 14 to 16)

nodes.t: M-03 Linked lists, trees and kernel data structures (weeks 17 to 19)

nodes.t: A-01 Registers, memory model and the first instruction (weeks 20 to 22)

nodes.t: A-02 Instructions: data movement, arithmetic, logic, jumps (weeks 23 to 25)

nodes.t: A-03 Stack frames, function calls and the ABI in assembly (weeks 26 to 28)
nodes.tiny: Draw a stack frame for one call

nodes.t: R-01 ELF binary format: the structure of Linux executables (weeks 29 to 31)

nodes.t: R-02 Static analysis: Ghidra, radare2, objdump (weeks 32 to 35)

nodes.t: R-03 Dynamic analysis: GDB, strace, ltrace, ptrace (weeks 36 to 38)

ladders.name: Coding and OSS to GSoC 2027
ladders.src: roadmap.html (3 CP phases, OSS stages 0 to 3)

nodes.t: CP phase 1: Codeforces setup, A-rated problems, core patterns, C++ STL, first Div. 3 round
nodes.tiny: Register on Codeforces and open problem A

nodes.t: CP phase 2: graphs, BFS, DFS, Dijkstra, Bellman-Ford (30+ problems)
nodes.tiny: Write BFS from memory

nodes.t: CP phase 2: dynamic programming from 1D to bitmask
nodes.tiny: Solve one coin change problem

nodes.t: CP phase 2: greedy with proof first, plus weekly rounds and upsolving
nodes.tiny: Read the editorial of your last unsolved problem

nodes.t: CP milestone: Codeforces Specialist, rating 1200 to 1400
nodes.tiny: Look up your current rating

nodes.t: CP phase 3: segment trees, DSU, tries, lazy propagation
nodes.tiny: Code a DSU with path compression

nodes.t: CP phase 3: number theory and combinatorics (mod p, sieve)
nodes.tiny: Write modular exponentiation

nodes.t: CP milestone: Codeforces Expert 1600+ with 2 virtual contests a week
nodes.tiny: Pick a virtual contest at your difficulty ceiling

nodes.t: OSS stage 0: Git, a professional GitHub profile, how an OSS project works, first docs PR
nodes.tiny: Write your profile README

nodes.t: OSS stage 1: pick your stack, find projects, go deep on one or two
nodes.tiny: Open goodfirstissue.dev and bookmark 3 issues

nodes.t: OSS stage 1: 5 to 10 merged PRs with clear commit messages and PR descriptions
nodes.tiny: Open one issue you want to fix

nodes.t: OSS stage 2: study the GSoC org list, narrow to 2 or 3 orgs, contact mentors
nodes.tiny: List 5 orgs that match your stack

nodes.t: OSS stage 2: become a known contributor, learn the toolchain, 20+ merged PRs and 2 features
nodes.tiny: Run the test suite of your target project

nodes.t: OSS stage 3: harder issues and reviewing other PRs
nodes.tiny: Read one open PR and leave a useful comment

nodes.t: OSS stage 3: validate your project idea with a mentor
nodes.tiny: Write the idea in 5 lines

nodes.t: OSS stage 3: write the proposal: about you, the problem, a week-by-week timeline, deliverables
nodes.tiny: Write the proposal outline with 4 headings

nodes.t: OSS stage 3: submit the proposal and keep contributing during selection
nodes.tiny: Open one issue and comment on it
